rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should test a baseline multimodal configuration to establish performance benchmarks. This experiment tests combining RNA (PCA) and image (ResNet50) data with simple concatenation fusion, isolating the effect of multimodal integration. It is the best use of the first experiment as it directly addresses the core challenge of multimodal cellular profiling without overcomplicating the setup.

The existing evidence shows that config_016 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, concat fusion) achieves 52.66% accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from 'concat' to 'weighted' improves performance, isolating the impact of fusion strategy. It is the best next step as it directly compares a key design choice (fusion) within the same model setting and profile setting, offering high potential to improve accuracy without overcomplicating the configuration.

Existing evidence shows multimodal singleprofile models with concat fusion (0.526 accuracy) are slightly better than weighted fusion (0.523). This experiment tests multiprofile with avgpool aggregation and concat fusion, isolating the effect of profile setting (single vs multi) and aggregation method. It balances exploration of multiprofile (a key design choice) with reuse of effective components (resnet50, concat) from prior experiments.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile setups with avgpool aggregation and concat fusion (config_018) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.618). This experiment tests whether switching to weighted fusion (instead of concat) in the same multiprofile setup improves accuracy, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. It is the best next step as it builds on the strongest current configuration while exploring a key design choice with minimal changes.

The existing evidence shows that multiprofile and weighted fusion yield higher accuracy (config_019: 0.639). This experiment tests whether transformer aggregation (vs. avgpool) further improves performance while keeping RNA encoder, image encoder, and fusion method consistent. It isolates the effect of aggregation, a key design choice, to determine if more complex aggregation methods outperform simpler ones.

The existing evidence shows that multiprofile multimodal models with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_019) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.639). This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l (a stronger vision transformer) could further improve performance, while keeping RNA encoder, aggregation, and fusion consistent. This isolates the impact of the image representation, a critical design choice, with minimal changes to the proven effective configuration.

The existing evidence shows that multiprofile, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (as in config_019 and config_025) yield the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 in this high-performing setup improves accuracy, isolating the impact of the RNA encoder choice. It balances exploitation of the current top setup with exploration of a potentially better encoder.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_031) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.6776). This experiment tests whether using the more powerful imagenet_vit_l image encoder (instead of resnet50) with the same RNA encoder and fusion method could further improve performance. It isolates the impact of the image encoder choice, which is critical for multimodal models, and leverages the strong foundation of the current best configuration.

The existing evidence shows config_037 (scvi_n200, avgpool, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.706). This experiment tests scgpt RNA encoder with the same image encoder (imagenet_vit_l), aggregation (avgpool), and fusion (weighted) to isolate the impact of RNA encoder choice. It directly compares a more advanced encoder (scgpt) against the current best (scvi_n200) while keeping other factors constant, which is critical for determining if this design choice can further improve performance.

The existing evidence shows config_037 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy (0.7062). This experiment tests transformer aggregation with the same RNA and image encoders but weighted fusion, which could improve performance by leveraging transformer's capacity for complex interactions. It clarifies whether transformer aggregation outperforms avgpool in this setup, directly comparing key design choices without changing other factors.
